title: 17 — Personal Data and India's DPDP Act
html:
17 — Personal Data and India's DPDP Act

The one idea: financial documents carry personal data (names, PAN, phone numbers, signatures) even when the platform only wants company facts. India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act and its 2025 Rules turn "handle it carefully" into dated legal duties. Design for them now: know where personal data is, keep only what you need, and redact before it travels.

This note explains engineering consequences. It is not legal advice; confirm obligations with your legal team.

1. What it is

  • DPDP Act, 2023: India's personal-data law. It covers digital personal data processed in India, and processing outside India connected with offering goods or services to people in India.
  • DPDP Rules, 2025: notified on 13 November 2025, with a phased start:
Date What starts (per multiple legal summaries, checked 2026-10-26)
13 Nov 2025 Definitions and the Data Protection Board framework
13 Nov 2026 Registration of Consent Managers
13 May 2027 Most substantive duties: notice, consent, security safeguards, breach reporting, rights of data principals, duties of Significant Data Fiduciaries, cross-border rules, children's data

Some media reports suggested the May 2027 date could be brought forward to November 2026. Check the official gazette before planning against either date.

Term Meaning
Data principal The person the data is about
Data fiduciary Whoever decides why and how personal data is processed
Data processor Processes on a fiduciary's behalf
Significant Data Fiduciary (SDF) A fiduciary designated for volume or risk, with extra duties (such as audits and impact assessments)
Consent Manager A registered intermediary through which people give, manage and withdraw consent

2. Why it matters

  • Annual reports, rating rationales and filings name individuals: directors, promoters, auditors, compliance officers. Some carry PAN, addresses or signatures.
  • Collecting company data for analytics can still mean processing personal data, which brings notice, purpose, retention and security duties, unless an exemption applies (legal will advise).
  • Sending pages to an outside model is processing by a third party, and possibly a cross-border transfer.

3. The main ideas

3.1 Engineering duties that follow

Duty (simplified) What the platform does
Know what you hold Classify columns and documents (governed tags such as pii.pan, pii.person_name). Unity Catalog's automated data classification can help
Purpose and minimisation Extract the company facts you need, and don't copy personal fields into Silver or Gold unless a purpose requires them
Security safeguards Masks and row filters on personal columns, encryption, access logs, least privilege
Retention and erasure Retention dates per dataset. Be able to find and remove a person's data (see the GDPR erasure section in orchestration and governance)
Breach reporting Audit logs good enough to say what was exposed, to whom, and when
Rights of data principals Find a person's records across tables, with lineage
Outside processing Redact before any external model call, and record the processor and the purpose

3.2 Immutable landing versus erasure

Immutable, WORM landing (keep every byte, locked) and erasure duties pull in opposite directions. Common patterns, to agree with legal:

  • Classify at landing. Keep files with personal data in a separate, restricted volume with its own retention.
  • Redacted working copies. Pipelines read a redacted derivative, so the locked original is touched only for audit.
  • Retention periods on the WORM policy that match the legal basis, rather than "forever".
  • Crypto-shredding, where suitable: encrypt per subject and destroy the key to make data unreadable.
---
title: Personal data path through a document pipeline
---
flowchart LR
    F["Landed file<br/>(restricted volume, retention set)"] --> C["Classify<br/>(person names, PAN, phone, email)"]
    C --> R["Redacted working copy"]
    R --> X["Extraction of company facts"]
    X --> S["Silver / Gold<br/>(no personal fields unless needed)"]
    C -. "needed personal fields only" .-> P["Restricted table<br/>masks + row filters + retention"]
    R --> EXT["Outside model (only if allowed)<br/>via gateway, logged"]

4. Working code

This chapter has no new code. The redaction example in the document intelligence module masks personal PAN, phone and email while keeping a corporate PAN. Pair it with a column mask in Unity Catalog (05).

5. Common mistakes

  1. "We only collect company data." Filings name people. Classify before deciding.
  2. Copying director details into every product table. Keep them in one restricted table and join only when the purpose needs them.
  3. WORM with no retention plan. Agree retention and erasure patterns with legal before locking.
  4. Unlogged outside model calls. You can't report or limit what you didn't record.
  5. Planning only for May 2027. Consent Manager registration starts in November 2026, and dates may move.

6. Exercise (45 minutes)

List every personal field that could appear in a factsheet, an annual report and a rating rationale. For each one, decide keep, redact or restrict, write the governed tag you would apply, and the purpose that justifies keeping it.

7. Questions to test yourself

  1. When were the DPDP Rules notified, and when do most substantive duties start?
  2. What is the difference between a data fiduciary and a data processor?
  3. Why can an outside model call raise DPDP questions?
  4. How can immutable landing coexist with erasure duties?
  5. Which Unity Catalog features help with "know what you hold"?

Answers

  1. Notified on 13 November 2025. Most substantive duties start on 13 May 2027, per the phased schedule (possibly earlier, per media reports).
  2. The fiduciary decides why and how data is processed. The processor acts on the fiduciary's behalf.
  3. It is processing by a third party, possibly cross-border, and needs a purpose, safeguards and a record.
  4. Restricted volumes with set retention, redacted working copies, and crypto-shredding where suitable, all agreed with legal.
  5. Automated data classification and governed tags, with ABAC masks on tagged columns.

8. Sources

Checked 2026-10-26 through web search. Legal summaries, not the gazette text, so confirm with the official notification.

  • DPDP Rules, 2025 (overview): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_Personal_Data_Protection_Rules,_2025
  • Legal 500, phased commencement: https://www.legal500.com/intelligence/india/privacy/india's-digital-personal-data-protection-act-and-the-dpdp-rules-2025-phased-commencement-core-obligations-and-a-board-ready-compliance-strategy
  • LKS, compliance timeline: https://www.lkslaw.com/insights/articles/dpdp-act-and-rules-a-ticking-compliance-timeline
  • Ministry of Electronics and IT: https://www.meity.gov.in
